faq.a: Yes — version 4 UUIDs generated with your browser's cryptographic random source (crypto.getRandomValues), the same mechanism used by professional tools.
In practice, no. A v4 UUID has 122 random bits; you would need to generate billions before a collision becomes remotely plausible.
faq.q: Can two generated UUIDs ever collide?

whenNotToUse: UUIDs are identifiers, not secrets — don't use them as passwords, tokens, or anything an attacker must not guess in security-critical flows without rate limiting.
If your database or spec needs a different UUID version (time-ordered v7, namespace-based v3/v5), this generator only produces random v4 values.
